extraction_notes: Real frames decoded from imports/source_videos/active/shinkai/SHINKAI_01.mp4 (imageio+ffmpeg, confirmed h264, 1920x1080, 24fps, duration 90.07s). Source file is an official 'Your Name' (Kimi no Na wa) theatrical trailer -- every frame carries a permanent title-logo (top-left) and release-date text (top-right) overlay, and many frames carry dialogue subtitles (bottom). Per standing instruction, overlays were ignored for measurement except where they materially obscure the subject; overlay_present/overlay_obscures_subject are recorded per candidate. Like GHIBLI_01, this trailer cuts extremely rapidly -- re-sampling at 0.3-0.5s spacing across all 4 scene windows found each nominal window (themselves still estimated, not real) actually spans 2-4 distinct shots, not one continuous shot. Static-property candidates (emotion_state, location_anchor, lighting_state, subject_position, shot_scale, camera_angle, blocking) were measured from a single real anchor frame at or near each window's start, which is a valid single-frame read regardless of the surrounding montage. The one motion-dependent candidate (camera_motion, cc_007) required locating a genuinely continuous sub-shot via finer sampling (found at 24.1-24.5s, a hair-tie macro insert) rather than the window's nominal start/end, which straddle a cut. transition_hint (cc_009) was confirmed directly by comparing frames straddling a real observed cut. All 12 candidates are REAL measurements; none are fabricated or guessed.

coordinate_candidates.note: Character's face shows wide eyes, open mouth, and a visible sweat drop while staring at a phone -- a shocked/distressed expression, not neutral.
Indoor classroom/study setting -- desk, books, pen cup, ceiling light fixture directly visible. Opposite of the prior exterior estimate.

A desk lamp produces a crisp highlight on the character's hair with a defined shadow edge under the chin/collar -- a harder lighting quality than the prior mixed estimate. Confidence medium given lighting-quality judgments are inherently more subjective than positional measurements.
Primary subject (a boy on a rooftop/bridge at sunset) occupies the left third of the frame, with open sky and background cranes filling the right two-thirds -- not centered as previously estimated.
Waist-up framing directly confirmed. Matches the prior estimate.
Camera sits at or slightly below the subject's head height with a large expanse of open sky above him -- a low angle looking up, opposite of the prior high-angle estimate.

This window (23.81-31.5s) spans at least 4 distinct shots (confirmed via re-sampling at 23.81/24.1/24.5/25.0/27.5/29.88/30.3/30.8/31.5s: dark landscape, hair-tie macro, extreme close eye, moon/title card, crying-face close-up). The hair-tie macro insert is internally continuous from ~24.1s to ~24.5s: the framing visibly tightens around the same cord-knot action between the two frames -- a push-in, not the prior static estimate. Measured from this continuous sub-segment near the window's start, not the full window. Confidence medium: short 0.4s span.

Two figures' hands are directly interacting in a hair-tying action (one figure's hands tying a cord into another figure's hair) -- a direct pair exchange, categorized distinctly from a generic two-shot (which implies two figures merely co-present in frame rather than actively interacting).

Directly compared the frame at 23.81s (a near-black distant landscape with an approaching light) against 24.1s (a bright hair-tie macro insert) -- content, framing, and lighting are entirely unrelated between the two, confirming a hard cut rather than a match cut (which would require visual continuity carried across the cut).

This anchor frame is a night-sky/moon landscape shot with no character face in frame -- 'tense' here characterizes the overall scene mood (dark clouds, an on-screen 'this number does not exist' dialing-failure subtitle) rather than a measured facial expression. Confidence low because emotion_state is not directly readable from a character in this specific frame, unlike cc_001.
Night sky with moon and clouds directly confirmed. Matches the prior estimate.
Diffuse moonlight through clouds with no hard edges anywhere in frame -- a soft lighting quality, not mixed.

identity_safety.note: Only abstract categorical shot-grammar labels are recorded (shot scale, camera angle, positions, lighting/emotion category) -- no dialogue, character likeness detail, on-screen text, titles, or branding from the source trailer is reproduced anywhere in this file.

extraction_summary.completion_note: Static-property candidates were measured from single real anchor frames; the one motion-dependent candidate (cc_007) and the one transition candidate (cc_009) were measured from genuinely continuous/compared real frame pairs located via finer re-sampling. No value in this file was guessed or interpolated without a corresponding frame read.
